f5_probe:
CONFIRMED bypass (real gitleaks 8.30.1, git 2.52.0.windows.1; 20:49:00-20:51:17, about 2.5 min).

Setup: a scratch repo with the Phase A harness env and core.hooksPath=.githooks holding the current hook. A runtime GitHub-token shape was staged; only gitleaks knows this shape. Each case ran a REAL `git commit`.

Results:
- Plain commit: rc=1, not committed, 'gitleaks refused the staged changes (rule id and place above)'.
- `git -c color.ui=always commit`: rc=1, refused the same way.
- `git -c color.diff=always commit`: rc=0, COMMITTED.

Diagnosis, from the same window:
- f5_precedence.out: a git child of the hook sees GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS win over the hook's GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (`git config --get color.ui` = always even with the override).
- f5_direct.out: gitleaks run directly with GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS 'color.ui'='always' gives rc=0. With the hook's COUNT override added it gives rc=1 (github-pat).
- So color.ui=always fails only because the override's color.diff=never is more specific. A user color.diff=always wins.

The six regex shapes are unaffected, because the hook's own diffs pass --no-color. Per TBF17 this becomes a stated limit, the GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS patch goes to the follow-up issue, and nothing was applied. Not measured: the Linux 8.30.1 binary.

Outputs: fix3/f5_probe.out, f5_probe_diff.out, f5_precedence.out, f5_direct.out.
stated_limits: gitleaks is optional in the hook: when it is absent there is one WARNING and the commit proceeds. CI's secret-scan job is the mandatory scan. On a public repo that job is DETECTION, not prevention, and it is not a required check until the owner adds it in branch protection.
Without gitleaks, M2 stays open for shapes outside the six regex branches (e.g. py_compile echoes a GitHub token on a Python syntax-error line) (TB7, review 13).

A textconv command or an external diff (diff.external, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, a diff.<driver>.command) that FAILS refuses the commit with 'could not read the staged diff'; the base hook passed silently (review correction 1, TBF3).

When gitleaks 8.30.1 logs an ERR line and exits 0 (e.g. a textconv driver that writes to stderr while working), the commit is refused with 'run gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged by hand' (TBF1, fail-closed). The hook never prints gitleaks' stderr, because an ERR line can quote git's stderr.

The TBF1 test is the substring ' ERR ' on gitleaks' --no-color log at log level error, the same test as the CI step (which now also runs gitleaks with --no-color, TBF11). A future gitleaks that changes its level text or ignores --no-color is guarded only by its exit code and report.

The backstop uses the base selection (no header state): with a dead awk, an added line whose CONTENT starts with `++` is seen only by the backstop and is skipped there, exactly as the base hook skipped it; with a working awk the two readers above catch it. (TBF14; replaces the deleted fix-2 limit about an awk that dies on the file.)

With gitleaks installed, `git -c color.diff=always commit` defeats the hook's colour override for gitleaks' own git diff. git exports GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, which git applies after the hook's GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. gitleaks then finds nothing. Measured with 8.30.1: a staged GitHub-token shape was committed (rc 0). `git -c color.ui=always` alone does not bypass (the override's color.diff=never is more specific). The six regex shapes are unaffected (the hook's own diffs use --no-color). The GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS patch is in the follow-up issue (TBF17, F5).

Content at an ALLOWLISTED asset path that carries the right magic bytes (UTF-16, NUL or attribute-binary) is regex-scanned only as far as --text exposes ASCII runs, and never for UTF-16. A secret inside an allowlisted image is never read (TB14).

Attribute-forced text (an untracked .gitattributes, or .git/info/attributes with `diff`) and UTF-16 with no NUL in its first 8,000 bytes pass the binary refusal. The regex checks still read the --text view (TBF4, #317).

The binary refusal covers PDF, archives, office files, databases and executables, and images or fonts outside the TB3 rows (e.g. landing/ OG images, tests/fixtures images, test_images/*.jpg, a UTF-16 .ps1). Each stays refused until its path is allowlisted in .githooks/pre-commit in its own commit (TB3, adversary A5).

A work-tree .gitleaksignore is refused only when gitleaks is installed; with gitleaks absent, a committed one is caught by the CI guard (TBG3). The hook's gitleaks always reads HEAD's .gitleaks.toml or a default-only file, never the working tree's (TBF2). `--no-verify` bypasses every check (TB14).
CI reads .gitleaks.toml from the range base, so an allowlist change must land in its own PR first.
A clean `git merge` runs no pre-commit hook. A concluded conflicted merge runs it over the whole merged-in diff, with no MERGE_HEAD exemption (TB9).
`git commit --amend` scans only the delta against the amended commit (pre-existing; applies to every check).

ESLint: with more than 10 partially staged client files, their working copies are linted (NOTE). By-path ESLint calls take at most 64 paths (TBF5 c, TBF13).
